options.A_keep_the_proxy_and_the_registered_with: current state. Pfizer, Lumen and Paramount D02 stay withdrawn by name; the other eight positions are unaffected. No meaning change and no new call.
options.B_narrow_to_titled_contingency_notes: a change to what D02 means: it drops the policy-note, acquisition-note and basis-of-presentation disclosures listed above from every filing that has them. It would deliver the three withdrawn positions by delivering less than the approved source asks for.
options.C_semantic_review_of_item_8_keyword_bloc: a per-block review - 'does this block disclose a legal proceeding, claim or loss contingency of the registrant or a subsidiary?' - over only the Item 8 blocks the keyword admits: 24 here. It adds a model stage to a route that is deterministic today, which is a new call type and needs a budget; #47 holds none.

question: Item 8 blocks outside an incorporated note reach D02 only through the _LEGAL keyword. Across the eleven filings with a D02 set that admits 24 blocks: 19 disclose a legal proceeding, claim or loss contingency of the registrant or a subsidiary, 5 mention litigation incidentally. Can a deterministic rule take the 5 out without taking any of the 19?
recommendation: A now. C if these three positions are to be delivered; B is not recommended because it trades a registered error for an unregistered loss.

keyword_inside_an_enumeration_is_inciden.reading: refuted before: Macy's 1065 lists 'losses, settlements, litigation costs and other factors' and discloses the registrant's own liability-claim accruals
keyword_inside_an_enumeration_is_inciden.rule: drop a block whose only keyword sits in a comma-separated list or a parenthetical

registrant_is_the_subject_of_a_legal_pre.reading: loses Southwest 1584 and 1585, which continue the class-action narrative without restating the subject, and Paramount 1900, which states the liabilities rather than the registrant's status
registrant_is_the_subject_of_a_legal_pre.rule: keep a block only when the registrant or a subsidiary is subject to, party to, a defendant in, or accrues for claims

title_names_contingencies_litigation_or_.reading: removes all five and loses four disclosures the approved source names: Macy's interchange-fee litigation settlement and its self-insured liability claims, Southwest's Winter Storm Elliott investigations, and Paramount's $1.4 billion of assumed asbestos and environmental contingent liabilities. Pfizer's Seagen bullet survives only if the bullet's own 'Legal Matters' label counts as a title.
title_names_contingencies_litigation_or_.rule: keep an Item 8 keyword block only when the note or subsection title it sits under names contingencies, litigation, legal proceedings or legal matters

standing_disposition_and_review_2026_09_.model_review_if_taken: Option C needs a concrete new call application naming the calls, and a review limited to the 24 blocks the keyword admits answers only the inclusion side. It must also cover the omission side - Item 8 blocks outside incorporated notes that the keyword never admits - or it cannot show the set is complete.
standing_disposition_and_review_2026_09_.what_the_measurements_show: Three measured deterministic rules each fail on a real filing here. That shows these three rules do not work; it does not show that no deterministic rule can.
standing_disposition_and_review_2026_09_.withdrawal: The three withdrawals (Pfizer, Lumen, Paramount 2025) and the predecessor-2024 instance are the current disposition under the existing rule that a value found wrong is not delivered. They are not a new decision for the owner, and the repair responsibility stays with the executor.

what_is_missing: Not a meaning. The approved source - Item 3, legal proceedings, contingencies notes - already classifies all 24 blocks, and the reading above did so against it. What no measured deterministic rule does is tell a block that discloses a legal matter from a block that mentions litigation on the way to something else; the three rules each fail on a real filing here.
